metadata.case_name: LAU TAT WING v. LO OI MING AND ANOTHER

source: On 10 December 2013, the day of the Alleged Collision, P visited the A&E department of the Hospital and was provisionally diagnosed with a sprained neck.
injuries.icd_description: Strain or sprain of cervical spine, unspecified

injuries.description: injury to the right upper limb
source: On 13 December 2013, P visited the A&E department of the Hospital and was provisionally diagnosed with an injury to the right upper limb.
On 18 December 2013, P visited the A&E department of the Hospital and was provisionally diagnosed with right hand pain.
injuries.icd_description: Injuries to the wrist or hand, unspecified

manifestations.description: Intermittent needle prick sensations to his neck and right hand, especially upon exertion
Occasional neck pain and soreness, with intermittent pain radiating to his upper limbs causing numbness
Easy fatigue and inability to move heavy objects

treatments_received.treatment: Attendance at Accident and Emergency Department of Pok Oi Hospital on 3 occasions
source: P received medical treatment at the Accident and Emergency Department (“A&E”) of Pok Oi Hospital (the “Hospital”) on 3 occasions, obtaining sick leave from 10 December 2013 to 20 December 2013.

treatments_received.treatment: Chinese bone-setting treatment (跌打) - several visits to a Chinese doctor
source: P further explained that he did not undergo any physiotherapy treatment but went to see a Chinese doctor several times for bone-setting treatment (跌打).

comparable_cases.case_name: Wong Pou Yin Kennie v Maxim’s Caterers Ltd
